The Covid-19 pandemic impacted the music and arts community particularly hard. Musicians who had previously been interviewed for the Fillius Jazz Archive graciously shared their experiences during this virtual shutdown period.
Butch was interviewed via Zoom on October 9, 2020, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive at Hamilton College and I’m very pleased to have a re-visit with drummer Butch Miles. Thanks for joining me today.
I’m very happy to be here, Monk, thank you for asking me.
So it was 25 years and 8 months since our last interview.
I kept doing the math. It was at the Paradise Valley Jazz Party.
Yeah. I remember that was Don and Sue Miller’s Jazz party in Paradise Valley, yeah.
And I recall you came for your interview right after walking off an upbeat set of music and you described yourself as a charter member of the Elvin Jones school of perspiration.

That’s very true. That was my introductory line because I used to — shall we say for the genteel crowd, I would perspire quite a bit. I don’t seem to do that that much anymore because I don’t seem to have much occasion to play that hard anymore.
